question: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}3&2&0\\ 1&4&0\\ 0&0&5\end{bmatrix},$ then compute $A^{2}-7A+10~I$
explanation:
Step 1 First, compute the squared matrix term $A^2 = A \cdot A$. We multiply matrix $A$ by itself: $\begin{bmatrix}3&2&0\\ 1&4&0\\ 0&0&5\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}3&2&0\\ 1&4&0\\ 0&0&5\end{bmatrix}$.

Step 2 Perform the matrix row-by-column dot product operations: for row 1 we calculate $[3(3)+2(1), 3(2)+2(4), 0] = [11, 14, 0]$. For row 2 we compute $[1(3)+4(1), 1(2)+4(4), 0] = [7, 18, 0]$. For row 3 we obtain $[0, 0, 5(5)] = [0, 0, 25]$. This gives us $A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 11 & 14 & 0 \\ 7 & 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 25 \end{bmatrix}$.

Step 3 Compute the scalar multiplication matrix $7A$ by multiplying every element inside matrix $A$ by the factor 7: $7A = \begin{bmatrix} 21 & 14 & 0 \\ 7 & 28 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 35 \end{bmatrix}$.

Step 4 Define the identity matrix product $10I$ scaled for a $3 \times 3$ matrix structure: $10I = \begin{bmatrix} 10 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 \end{bmatrix}$.

Step 5 Combine all these derived components into the expression $A^2 - 7A + 10I$: $\begin{bmatrix} 11 & 14 & 0 \\ 7 & 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 25 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 21 & 14 & 0 \\ 7 & 28 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 35 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 10 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 10 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 11-21+10 & 14-14 & 0 \\ 7-7 & 18-28+10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 25-35+10 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$. The result is a zero matrix.
